terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here and read what it prints.

tasks.title: Print the welcome
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/first-line.js`, print this line:

```
Welcome to Wickhollow Candles
```

Check runs your file with `node src/first-line.js` and looks for a line that matches this one exactly, capital letters and spaces included.
nextSteps: Run `node src/first-line.js` once and read what it prints today.
Look at the first `console.log` line in the file: it is your model.
Write a new line under `// Task 1` that prints the welcome.
Run the file again and compare the output with the task.
hints: The file already prints one line. Read how that line is written.
Text has to sit inside quotes, and the quotes sit inside the round brackets of `console.log`.
The line has the shape `console.log('...')`, with the welcome where the dots are.

tasks.title: Print the parcel note
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, print the two lines of the note that goes in every parcel, in this order:

```
Thank you for your order
Poured by hand in Wickhollow
```

Check runs your file and looks for both lines, the second right after the first.
nextSteps: Find `// Task 2` and read the two lines in the comment.
Print the first line with its own `console.log`.
Print the second line on the line below it.
Run the file and read the output from top to bottom.
hints: One `console.log` prints one line. How many lines does the note have?
Node runs your lines from the top of the file to the bottom, so the order you write them in is the order they print in.
Two `console.log` lines, one under the other, each with one line of the note in quotes.

tasks.title: Switch off the old offer
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3` there is a line that prints an offer the shop no longer runs. Turn it into a comment, so it stays in the file but no longer runs.

Check runs your file to see that the offer is not printed, then reads the file to see that the line is still there as a comment.
nextSteps: Run the file and find the offer in the output.
Find the line under `// Task 3` that prints it.
Turn that one line into a comment. Do not delete it.
Run the file again: the offer should be gone from the output.
hints: The lesson shows a way to keep a line in the file while Node skips it.
Every comment in this file starts the same way. Look at the start of the lines that do not print anything.
Put `//` at the very start of the offer's line.

tasks.title: Leave a note for Theo
tasks.description:
Write a comment of your own anywhere in `src/first-line.js`: a line that starts with `//`, followed by a few words for Theo, for example what the file prints.

Check reads your file and looks for a comment that was not there when you started. The file must still run.
nextSteps: Pick a place for your note, for example under `// Task 4`.
Write a few words after it.
Run the file: your note should not change what it prints.
hints: A comment is for people. Node skips it, so you can write anything in it.
A comment starts with two slashes. Everything after them on that line is skipped.
A line like `// Theo, ...` with a short sentence after it is all it takes.
